pages.title: Krishnadevaraya-era 1518 inscription sinking at Vankeswara temple, Palnadu

facts.text: Where: Vankeswara temple, Durgi mandal HQ, Palnadu district
facts.head: News

facts.text: Date: 22 November 1518 CE, reign of Sri Krishnadevaraya (Vijayanagara)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Commissioned by: Timmapa Nayanim Garu, a doorkeeper in the royal court
facts.head: News

facts.text: Records: grant of Gundala village for temple festivities
facts.head: News

facts.text: Text: 55 lines classical Telugu — only top 19 visible
facts.head: News

facts.text: Inspected by: E. Sivanagireddy, CEO, Pleach India Foundation (tip from sculptor Ch. Srinivasachary)
facts.head: News

pages.title: Srisailam copper plates (1420 CE) — first use of 'Swarajya' in a Telugu inscription

facts.text: Date: Saka 1341, Sarvari, Magha Sudha Trayodasi = 28 January 1420 CE
facts.head: News

facts.text: ⚠ Headline says 14th century but 1420 CE is 15th century
facts.head: News

facts.text: Format: three copper leaves, bilingual — Sanskrit and Telugu
facts.head: News

facts.text: Term: 'Swarajya Punarudhharana' (restoration of independent state) — ⚠ first-time use in a Telugu inscription (per Dr K. Munirathnam Reddy, Director (Epigraphy), ASI Mysore)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Ruler: Recharla Lingama Nayaka (Recharla dynasty) — reclaimed areas from the Turakas; restored eight agraharas
facts.head: News

facts.text: Services restored: Nityaapahara, Akhanda-Dipala-Chamuru, Nityasatram, Sivaratri Mahotsavam, Bhuri Satram
facts.head: News

facts.text: Bal Gangadhar Tilak: "Swarajya is my birthright"
facts.head: Link to freedom movement

facts.text: Tanguturi Prakasam started the newspaper 'Swarajya' in three languages
facts.head: Link to freedom movement
